name: Creating digital products
intro: How to plan, create, edit and publish digital products in English that combine text, pictures, video and sound, from podcasts and videos to websites and infographics.
sammendrag:
## Digital products

A **digital product** is something you create with digital tools that combines different **media types**: text, pictures, video, sound, animation and interactive elements. Examples are a podcast, a short film, a website, a digital poster, a slideshow, an animation, a vlog or a digital story.

## Start with purpose and audience

Before choosing tools, ask:

- **Purpose**: Do you want to inform, explain, tell a story, persuade or entertain?
- **Audience**: Who is it for? Classmates, younger pupils or a global audience?
- **Message**: What is the one thing you want the audience to remember?

## Choose the right format

- A **podcast** suits interviews, discussions and storytelling with sound.
- A **video** is good for showing actions, places and emotions.
- A **website** or blog can combine long texts, pictures and links.
- An **infographic** presents facts and numbers visually.
- A **digital story** combines narration, pictures and music into a short personal story.

## Plan your product

1. **Brainstorm** ideas and research your topic.
2. Write a **script** or outline: What will be said and shown?
3. Make a **storyboard** – simple sketches of each scene or page.
4. Collect or create **material**: photos, recordings and music.
5. Make a **timeline** for the work, especially in group projects.

## Combining media types

Good digital products use media types that **support each other**:

- Pictures and text should say something together, not repeat each other word for word.
- Music should match the mood and not drown out speech.
- Use **captions** or subtitles to make videos accessible.
- Keep a **consistent design** with the same fonts, colours and style.
- Think about **accessibility**: readable text, good contrast and clear sound.

## Recording and editing

- Record sound in a quiet room, and keep the microphone close.
- Film with steady hands or a tripod, and use natural light.
- When **editing**, cut away mistakes and long pauses, use transitions sparingly and adjust the sound level.
- Watch or listen to the whole product before publishing.

## Feedback and publishing

Test your product on someone from the target audience and ask for **feedback**. Improve it before you publish. Remember:

- **Copyright**: use your own material or material you have permission to use, and credit your sources.
- **Privacy**: get **consent** from everyone who appears in your product.
- Think about **where** you publish: in class, on a school platform or openly online.

flashcards.def: Something created with digital tools that combines different media types.
Text, pictures, video, sound, animation and interactive elements.
What you want to achieve: inform, explain, tell, persuade or entertain.
The people your product is made for.
The main thing you want the audience to remember.
An audio programme, good for interviews, discussions and stories.
A visual presentation of facts and numbers.
A short personal story told with narration, pictures and music.
A written plan of what will be said and shown.
Simple sketches of each scene or page.
Text on screen that shows what is said.
Using the same fonts, colours and style throughout.
Making a product easy for as many people as possible to use.
Cutting, arranging and improving recorded material.
Permission from people who appear in your product.

options: A device used to create and store digital media files
A physical item designed with software and sold online
Something made with digital tools that combines different media types
A single media file created with one digital tool
quiz.explain: Podcasts, videos and websites are examples.

quiz.text: What should you decide before choosing tools?
options: Your purpose, audience and message
Your budget, device and editing software
Your format, file type and preferred platform
Your title, colour scheme and background music
quiz.explain: Purpose and audience decide which format fits best.

quiz.text: Which format is best for presenting facts and numbers visually?
options: A podcast
A photo essay
A short story
An infographic
quiz.explain: Infographics use charts, icons and short texts.

options: A set of finished photos showing each scene or page
A set of simple sketches showing each scene or page
A written list of dialogue for each scene or page
A list of camera equipment for each scene or page
quiz.explain: Storyboards help you plan before you record.

quiz.text: Why should you add captions to a video?
options: To make the video accessible to more people
To add background information that is not spoken aloud
To make the video play at a faster speed
To identify every person who appears on screen
quiz.explain: Captions help people who cannot hear the sound or are watching without it.

quiz.text: How should pictures and text work together?
options: They should repeat exactly the same information
They should focus on separate topics and avoid connecting
They should work together and support the same message
Pictures should decorate the page while text explains everything
quiz.explain: Each media type should add something.

quiz.text: What is a good tip for recording sound?
options: Record in a busy room with the microphone close
Record in a quiet room with the microphone far away
Record in a quiet room with music playing nearby
Record in a quiet room with the microphone close
quiz.explain: Clear sound is essential in podcasts and videos.

quiz.text: What must you get from people who appear in your video?
options: A filming schedule
Consent
A copy of the video
A copyright licence
quiz.explain: Everyone has the right to decide over pictures and videos of themselves.

options: A recorded file of what has already been said and shown
A list of fonts used in a digital product
A written plan of what will be said and shown
A visual plan made from sketches of each scene
quiz.explain: A script makes recording easier and more structured.

quiz.text: Why should you test your product on someone from the target audience?
options: To get feedback and improve it before publishing
To check whether the software works on your computer
To decide which tools to use before production begins
To make the finished product without editing it
quiz.explain: Feedback shows what works and what is unclear.

ekstra.text: Music should be loud enough to drown out the speech.
ekstra.explain: Music should support the speech, not compete with it.

ekstra.text: A consistent design uses the same fonts, colours and style.
ekstra.explain: Consistency makes a product look professional.

ekstra.text: A podcast can be a digital product.
ekstra.explain: Podcasts combine voice, music and sound effects.

ekstra.text: You don't need to credit sources in digital products.
ekstra.explain: All sources and borrowed material must be credited.

options: Making a product usable for as many people as possible
Making a product available to as many websites as possible
Making a product simple to publish on social media
Making a product easy to find in an online search
ekstra.explain: Good contrast, captions and clear sound improve accessibility.

ekstra.text: Which format suits interviews and discussions with sound?
options: An infographic
A podcast
A photo essay
A printed brochure

ekstra.text: What happens in the editing stage?
options: You choose a topic and define your audience
You write a script and plan the scenes
You cut away mistakes and adjust the sound
You record the footage and capture the sound
ekstra.explain: Editing turns raw recordings into a finished product.

skriv.text: A class is making a digital product for younger pupils. Explain the difference between its audience and its purpose, using this situation.
skriv.fasit: The audience is the younger pupils the product is made for. Its purpose is what the creators want to achieve, such as explaining something to them.
kriterier: Identifies the audience as the people the product is made for.
Explains that the purpose is what the creators want to achieve.

skriv.text: A student wants to make an interview about a school project. Compare how a podcast and a video could present the interview.
skriv.fasit: A podcast suits an interview because it uses sound. A video can also show the people, their actions and their emotions.
kriterier: Explains that a podcast is well suited to an interview because it uses sound.
Describes something a video can show that a podcast cannot, such as people or their actions.

skriv.text: When planning a short film, how do a script and a storyboard help in different ways?
skriv.fasit: A script plans what will be said and shown. A storyboard uses simple sketches to plan each scene.
kriterier: Explains that a script plans what will be said and shown.
Explains that a storyboard sketches out the scenes.

skriv.text: You want to tell a short personal story using narration, pictures and music. Explain why a digital story is a suitable format.
skriv.fasit: A digital story is suitable because it tells a short personal story using narration, pictures and music.
kriterier: Identifies the format as suitable for a short personal story.
Explains that it combines narration, pictures and music.

skriv.text: A website uses different fonts, colours and styles on every page. Suggest one design improvement and explain why it would help.
skriv.fasit: Use the same fonts, colours and style throughout the website. This creates a consistent design across its pages.
kriterier: Recommends using the same fonts, colours or style throughout.
Connects this choice to keeping the design consistent.

skriv.text: A video recording has mistakes, long pauses and music that is louder than the speech. Describe edits that would improve it.
skriv.fasit: Cut away the mistakes and long pauses, and adjust the sound level so the music does not drown out the speech.
kriterier: Suggests cutting mistakes or long pauses.
Suggests adjusting the sound so the speech can be heard over the music.

skriv.text: You plan to publish a video that shows a classmate and uses music made by someone else. What should you do about privacy and copyright?
skriv.fasit: Get the classmate’s consent before publishing the video. Use the music only if you have permission, and credit its source.
kriterier: Says to get consent from the classmate who appears in the video.
Says to have permission to use the music and credit its source.

skriv.text: You are filming a demonstration indoors, but the footage is shaky and dark. Name two filming choices that could improve the recording.
skriv.fasit: Hold the camera steadily or use a tripod. Use natural light to make the footage brighter.
kriterier: Suggests steady hands or a tripod to reduce shaky footage.
Suggests using natural light to improve the lighting.
